nonvacuity: Uniform law on Fin 6 with outcomes (0,1,2,3) and all six two-treated assignments is a positive finite design. For every B>0 take the probability measure assigning weight 1/(B+1)! to each vector (sigma(0),...,sigma(B)), sigma a permutation of 0,...,B, viewed in real coordinates. Composition permutes the atoms, proving exchangeability; every atom is injective. This works also at B=1000 and 10000, and alpha=1/20 satisfies the retained hypotheses. A distinct-coordinate vector for every B is constructed in scratch/Check.lean. For the finite-design clauses use the uniform law on the 12870 balanced assignments on 16 units and y_i=2^i. Independent exact enumeration found 6435 RSS values, every one on exactly two assignments. For B=1000 and 10000, independent 60- and 90-digit evaluations of the exact mixtures confirmed every strict comparison with 1/20; these numerical evaluations are supporting checks, not Lean proof certificates.

For the exchangeable-reference hypotheses, a Dirac probability measure at the all-zero vector is exchangeable and allows ties; an instance compiles in scratch/Check.lean. The uniform-permutation law on the distinct vector 0,...,B gives a nonconstant tie-free instance too. The iid clause permits, for example, weights (1,0) on a two-point space. Its exact-tail conjunct instead admits uniform weights on Fin 6. The disclosed strict-positive-weight convention is a restriction relative to generic clause (e), although it is already the premise of the clause's explicit reference to canonical T12(iii); it causes no loss when designs are represented on their positive support.

Take n=2, Y=(2,4), z=01, t=1, t'=2, a=2 and a'=3. Each group has size 1, the treated outcome is nonzero and both multiplicative parameters are nonzero and distinct. Take z=0011, t=10, Y=(0,1,12,13). Its adjusted vector is u=(0,1,2,3), both groups have size 2, the corrected contrast is 2, and the diagnostic imputed-treated contrast and raw observed contrast are both 12. More generally any adjusted u is realized by Y_i=u_i+z_i*t, so the let-bound adjustment does not restrict the domain of adjusted outcomes.

The constructed 256-unit calibrationY and calibrationZ supply the instance without assumptions. Both group sizes equal 128; those equalities compile in scratch/Check.lean. Nonnegativity for every parameter follows because every discrepancy is an absolute value and the median averages in-bounds nonnegative order statistics.
